# Break down complex news stories into easy-to-understand points with Grok

Ever felt overwhelmed by a news article full of jargon or lengthy explanations? This guide will show you how to use Grok, an AI assistant, to quickly summarise news stories into clear, concise points. By the end, you'll be able to get the gist of any article in minutes, helping you stay informed without the struggle.

## Before you start
- An active X (formerly Twitter) account.
- An active X Premium+ subscription, as Grok is currently an exclusive feature for these members.
- The X app on your mobile device or access to the X website on a computer.
- Roughly 5-10 minutes to follow along and try it out.

## Step 1 — Open Grok
First, you'll need to open the Grok AI assistant. If you're on a computer, open your web browser and go to X.com. If you're using a mobile device, open the X app. On the left-hand side of the screen (or along the bottom menu bar if you're on mobile), look for an icon that looks like a stylised 'X' or 'Grok' text. Tapping or clicking this will launch Grok. If you don't see it, ensure you're logged into your X Premium+ account, as Grok is an exclusive feature. You'll know it worked when the Grok chat interface appears on your screen, often with a welcome message.

## Step 2 — Start a new conversation
Now that Grok is open, let's start fresh. Look for a button or icon that typically signifies starting a new chat, often found in the top-right corner or bottom-centre of the screen. This might look like a square with a pen icon, a plus (+) sign, or simply say "New Chat." Tapping this will clear any previous conversation and prepare Grok for your new request. If you can't find a "New Chat" button, you can often just type your request directly into the existing chat box, and Grok will treat it as a new topic. You'll know it worked when the chat history disappears (if there was any) and a blank text box appears at the bottom, ready for your input.

## Step 3 — Paste the news and give an instruction (prompt)
With a new conversation ready, find the news article you want to understand. Copy the entire article text or, even easier, just its web address (URL) from your browser. Paste this into Grok's text box at the bottom of the screen. Immediately after pasting, add your instruction, also known as a **prompt** (your specific request to the AI assistant). Make sure your instruction is clear about what kind of summary you want. Grok, like any **AI assistant** (a smart computer program designed to understand and respond to human language), needs precise guidance.
💬 Example: `Summarise this news article about the recent weather patterns in Sydney into five bullet points, explaining any jargon.`
You'll know it worked when Grok starts generating a response in the chat window, usually appearing line by line.

## Step 4 — Refine your summary
Sometimes Grok's first summary might not be exactly what you need. Perhaps it's too long, too technical, or doesn't focus on the specific details you're interested in. This is where refining your request comes in. After Grok provides its initial summary, you can simply type a follow-up instruction into the same chat box. Grok will remember the previous context (the article and your last request) and adjust its response accordingly. If it looks different, and Grok seems to have forgotten the context, simply re-paste the article and add a more specific prompt from the start.
💬 Example: `Can you make that simpler, as if explaining to a teenager, and focus only on the impact on daily life?`
You'll know it worked when Grok generates a new summary, incorporating your feedback and presenting the information in a different style or with a new focus.

## Step 5 — Ask follow-up questions
One of the great strengths of an AI assistant like Grok is its ability to engage in a conversation. Once you have a summary, you can ask follow-up questions to delve deeper into specific points or clarify anything that's still unclear. This lets you explore the topic at your own pace without having to reread the original article. For instance, if the summary mentioned a technical term, you could ask Grok to explain it in everyday language. If you accidentally close the chat, you might need to start a new conversation and re-paste the article, then ask your question.
💬 Example: `What exactly does 'atmospheric river' mean in simple terms, as mentioned in the article?`
You'll know it worked when Grok provides a concise answer to your specific question, drawing details from the article you provided earlier.

## Common mistakes
-   **Pasting only the headline**: If you only give Grok the headline, it won't have enough information to summarise the whole story.
    *   **The fix**: Always paste the full article text or, ideally, the complete web address (URL) so Grok can access all the details.
-   **Vague instructions**: Asking "Summarise this" without more detail might give you a generic response that isn't tailored to your needs.
    *   **The fix**: Be specific in your prompt. Say "Summarise this for a 10-year-old," or "List the three main pros and cons," or "Explain the impact on local businesses."
-   **Expecting Grok to access private content**: Grok can't read articles behind paywalls or from your private documents unless you manually paste the text into the chat.
    *   **The fix**: For paywalled articles, copy and paste the full text (if you have access) directly into Grok's chat window.

## What this means for you
-   **In everyday life:** You can quickly catch up on local or international news during your morning commute or lunch break without getting bogged down by details, keeping you informed and saving you time.
-   **For your business or work:** You can efficiently process industry news, competitor updates, or regulatory changes, getting the key takeaways instantly to inform your decisions without needing to read every lengthy report.
-   **If you're just getting started:** Pick any news article that looks interesting but a bit long. Use Grok to summarise it into three bullet points. See how much faster you grasp the main ideas!

## Try it now
Grab a link to a recent news article about something you're curious about. Go to Grok, paste the link, and type: "Summarise this article in three sentences, making it very easy to understand."
